# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Scottsford, New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- **Role:** farmer  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes stick out, leading Anne to consider him extremely ugly in those moments. After reuniting with his wife, he presents a remarkably neat and snug appearance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Outspoken, fussy, fidgety, and crusty, Mr. Harrison was initially known throughout Avonlea as an eccentric crank. He prides himself on telling the plain truth regardless of tact, though he is fundamentally kind, sympathetic, and sociable beneath his cantankerous exterior. He frequently smokes his pipe on his veranda and is hard to please, offering fastidious and unsparingly direct criticism.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041)_

## History

In early April, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved from Scottsford, New Brunswick. Living alone with a swearing parrot named Ginger and keeping no fixed meal schedules, he quickly gained a local reputation as an eccentric crank. His friendship with Anne Shirley began tumultuously when he flew into a rage over her stray Jersey cow, but the two soon became warm neighbors who frequently confided in each other. He hired young John Henry Carter to help around the farm, though the boy complained of irregular meals. Later, Mr. Harrison's estranged wife Emily unexpectedly rejoined him in Avonlea following the death of Ginger, leading him to shave, tidy up his house, attend church every Sunday, and become even friendlier. During Anne's college years, he served as a brutally honest critic of her writing, encouraging her to cut excessive descriptions and high-flown dialogue.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P3](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0003), [v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P10](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0010), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c25 P45](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0045), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c27 P9](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0009), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P41](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0041), [v3 c12 P45](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0045)_

## Background by volume

- visited Prince Edward Island as a boy  <sub>[v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his sister kept house for him  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- married Emily Scott and took a fortnight's wedding trip to St. John  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- separated from his wife due to domestic friction and her dislike of his parrot Ginger  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- kept bachelor's hall after his sister died  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- received the profane parrot Ginger from his dying brother, a sailor  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining the Cuthbert place  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> And I suppose you were scared to death to come here and tell me, after the fuss I made yesterday, hey? But you mustn’t mind me, I’m a terrible outspoken old fellow, that’s all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> I guess you’ve got a spice of temper, It goes with hair like yours, I reckon. Avonlea is a pretty decent place or I wouldn’t have located here; but I suppose even you will admit that it has some faults?  <sub>[v2 c3 P42](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0042)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room, I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Well, we’re going to miss you an awful lot, Emily and me. To be sure, Mrs. Lynde’ll be over there in your place. There ain’t nobody but a substitute can be found for them.  <sub>[v2 c30 P4](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0004)</sub>

> I daresay there’s been many a romance in Avonlea—and many a tragedy, too, But your folks ain’t like real folks anywhere. They talk too much and use too high-flown language. There’s one place where that Dalrymple chap talks even on for two pages, and never lets the girl get a word in edgewise. If he’d done that in real life she’d have pitched him.  <sub>[v3 c12 P45](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0045)</sub>
